utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. Can we have the appearances, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: If your Honours please, my name is Grant Niemann and I appear with my colleagues, Ms. McHenry, Mr. Turone and Mr. Khan for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Can we have appearances on the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, your Honours. I am Edina Residovic, representing Mr. Zejnil Delalic, along with Mr. Eugene O'Sullivan, law professor from Canada.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: Good morning, your Honours, I am Zeljko Olujic, representing Mr. Zdravko Mucic, along with my colleague, Mr. Michael Greaves.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: Good morning, your Honours, I am Salih Karabdic, attorney from Sarajevo, representing Mr. Hazim Delic, along with Mr. Tom Moran, attorney from Houston, Texas.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Good morning, your Honours, I am John Ackerman, I appear here on behalf of Mr. Esad Landzo. My co-counsel, Ms. Cynthia McMurrey, is unavoidably delayed this morning and probably will not be able to be with us until the afternoon session, if there is such a session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: What is the position this morning?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: We are ready to proceed with the documents, a continuation of what we were doing yesterday, if your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Then you may well proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do not know if you have noticed, but Mr. Landzo is not with us today. I have no indication from him whether he waives his presence here or not. I cannot do it myself. I therefore object to going forward without his presence. The rule is clear, that the defendant must be present at all stages of the proceeding. He has not waived his presence here today. I cannot waive it on his behalf. I have not had any conversation with him. I do not know what his situation is. I suspect there are people in the courtroom that know a great deal more about it than I do, but I very strongly object to going forward without his presence. There are matters coming up this morning that may directly affect him. I am without any instruction from him regarding those matters. There may be things that would come up in the presentation that he would like to communicate to me in terms of possible objections, things of that nature. I strongly object to the matter going forward without his presence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Prosecution is not aware of anything in relation to this and we are not able to assist your Honours. There is a possibility though your Honours that we could avoid the difficulty envisaged by Mr. Ackerman in terms of the documents, which may have the effect of making the proceedings run a little bit more smoothly anyway; namely that I could proceed without seeking to tender any of the documents and having individual argument on each document, go through and make my submission in relation to the totality of all the documents and materials that we seek to tender, and counsel is present, they can then raise their objections tomorrow or at such time if it is necessary for their clients to be here, Mr. Ackerman's client to be here, and then run the objection at the conclusion of my full submission. So it seems to me, your Honour, that we are really only dealing with matters of law in relation to documents which have been around for some considerable time, and have already been the subject of considerable testimony. It seems to me, your Honours, that if I was to proceed to make these submissions and continue to do so, through to the conclusion that then counsel could respond at a later stage and any issues that they wish to raise in relation to them could be raised at that stage, and could presumably be raised in the presence of their client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman, is this procedure acceptable to you?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: No, your Honour, I have no indication from my client that he is willing for any part of this process to go forward without his presence. I do not think there is a procedure that can go forward without his waiver of presence, based upon the rather strict language of the Rule of this Tribunal. If the court decides to proceed without his presence, then I would also ask leave to be excused, because I think it would be inappropriate for me to participate without him being here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I do not know whether you are listening to what the Prosecution said. All he was doing was to tender all the documents, make his submission, and then leave you to reply later on the basis of the documents you would have received. In that circumstance, you will find that no issue of fact arises out of that legal argument. Perhaps you might be able at the time you would reply to have consulted your client and have his views on what you want to say. If you have any considerable experience on the light of the Statute, made up your mind that as long as your client is not here you will not participate even in legal argument, it is your option. You will well consult your client and the Trial Chamber will adjourn to enable you and your client to decide when the Trial Chamber will sit. Perhaps the Registrar might be able to give us an idea of what is happening in the camp of the accused. (Pause). I suppose since the main problem with Mr. Ackerman is that you have not seen your client and you have not been able to discuss with him. You would want to have a discussion with him and see whether he will be able to come in by 2.30 in the afternoon, if that suits you. Or if that does not suit you, you will agree with him when you think he can come in for the Trial Chamber to sit.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, you are exactly right. I want to make my position very clear so that you all understand it fully. The right of a defendant to be present at his own trial is his own personal right. It is not a right that he may exercise through counsel, except of his own will. Until my client tells me that I have the right to stand before this Tribunal and waive his presence, I do not have that right. There is no way I can acquire that right except through him, because it is his personal right to be present that is implicated here. That right is not specific as to what is going on in the courtroom. Therefore, I cannot agree to anything going on in this Trial Chamber unless I have from my client a waiver of his being here during that proceeding. I have very little information about why he is not here, very little, precious little. So I have no idea what the status of his health is, I have no idea whether he can be here in a hour or tomorrow or when. Until I can find those things out and have communication with him, all I can do is tell you what I have told you, that I do not have authority from him to waive his presence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You have actually not replied to what I said. The Trial Chamber wishes to sit again at 2.30. Are you willing to see whether you can at that time consult him and let the Trial Chamber know when he will be able to come in. By now we have still not had any medical certificate excusing him, we have nothing in front of the Trial Chamber, so if by that time you still have nothing, then we will know what to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You can also take instructions from him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Of course, and I am perfectly willing to do that as soon as I can walk out of the door of this Trial Chamber. I will begin the effort to try to find out what his status is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: I think you had better start to do that when we adjourn.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I am perfectly willing to do that. This came to my attention maybe about 9.45 this morning, with very little time to find out what was going on. I think there was a lot of confusion about what is going on and I am still totally confused. I have no idea what his status is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: We are going through this process because Article 21 -- the right under Article 21 is not what can be exercised unreasonably, because if that exercise interferes with the exercise of justice, I think we will have a way of dealing with this. That is why you need to consult him, to see what can be done in the circumstance.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour is maybe suggesting, and I think you are, that what may be happening here is just a refusal by my client to come to court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: If that is what is happening, there certainly is a way to deal with that and it should be taken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: This is what I am saying. If you consult him and then we get the feedback and know what the position is then we will know how to conduct the remainder of the trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I am not only willing to do that but anxious.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, as I said earlier, we do not know anything about the situation in terms of why he is not here, but might I just say that if Mr. Ackerman was good enough to raise with his client the proposal that I have advanced, namely that I would submit the legal argument today and that if he is ill and anticipates being able to come later in the week, then legal argument from the Defence perspective would be presented at that stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann, can any proceedings be held in the absence of the accused, any proceedings of any sort at the trial?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I believe so, your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Let us have a look at Article 21, the right to be tried in his presence. So any proceedings which form part of the trial, they have to be held in his presence. That is the difficulty with which we are faced. Article 21.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I am not arguing that your Honours should proceed with the matter in terms of -- in the face of the fact that he may be ill and through no cause of his own he cannot be present. I am not trying to urge that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: We do not know why he is not present today.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I do not know why not. All I am saying --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: All proceedings must be held in his presence unless we find good justification for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I do not see the argument for his rights, the case is suspended while he is unable to be here. There is no dispute about that. He has a right to be here while the trial is going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, and he can do it through his counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He can, but he has to authorise his counsel. It is exactly what Mr. Ackerman is saying, "I must consult my client".

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: If he wants to be here, he has a right to be here. There is no doubt about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: All I wish to do, show your Honours was under Article 21, paragraph 4(d). It says: "He has the right to be tried in his presence, to defend himself in person or through assistance of counsel -- legal assistance of his own choosing." So if he chooses, he can instruct Mr. Ackerman. What your Honours are saying is it is impossible for him to do it, for the case to go on even if he instructs Mr. Ackerman that he wants him to participate in the events in his absence; my answer is he can do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He can waive his right, but this is his right, therefore no part of the proceedings can be held in his absence, unless he waives his right and authorises Mr. Ackerman to represent him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I am not arguing with that. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I ask just one question which has nothing to do with what we have discussed so far? Can we request that this communication with Mr. Landzo be conducted sooner rather than later, because our clients are waiting, and while these consultations are going on our clients are in conditions that are less than perfect, so that we may continue either as soon as possible or that our clients are returned to the detention unit, so would it be possible to obtain some kind of information within one hour? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I have suggested we come back at 2.30. At that time every necessary consultation must have been made and then we know what to do. I suppose you prefer a shorter time, I too would, but I am imagining that we might not be able to do that before that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I think the concern is that the defendants are going to be kept in the cells here until 2.30. The cells here are literally just holding cells and they are not places where you want to sit for four or five hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: They would not mind sitting in the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I am sure it is very comfortable for them, but that is Ms. Residovic's concern, that our clients are going to be kept here until 2.30 in the cells, which is not really very satisfactory. That is the concern.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Mr. Landzo has some mercy for his co-accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I am not even going to speculate. That is all I am bothered about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: We might devise something a little better than that. (Pause). Initially I was perhaps thinking that it might be possible both consultation and the ability of Landzo to attend the Trial Chamber today, but I think on the face of what is going on now, with nobody having a very good knowledge of what is happening, I think we might as well adjourn now until tomorrow morning at 10.00, instead of everybody having different types of discomfort between now and 2.30 and we come at 2.30 and we do not even know what is going on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: I hope this will not upset your programme.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I will also ask the Registry to find out what the position is. I think that is the way we have to solve the little difficulties which have cropped up.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, the information that I got this morning could even permit one to conclude that my client is not even conscious and so having any kind of communication with him until he is, of course, would be impossible. I do not know that that is the case, but that is an indication that I received this morning. I need you to know I have very little information, almost none.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I think the Trial Chamber will now rise and reassemble at 10.00 tomorrow morning. (10.30 am)

procedural_notes.text: (Hearing adjourned until 10.00 am the following day)
